paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God finishes what He promises, even when the person who carried the promise doesn't get to see the last step. The LORD tells Moses, "This is the land that I swore to give Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob…" and then lets him see it with his own eyes (Deuteronomy 34:4). Moses doesn't cross over. But the promise doesn't die with him, because it was never resting on Moses. It was resting on the LORD who swore it.

Now look at how the passage remembers Moses. It calls him "the servant of the LORD" (Deuteronomy 34:5), and it says the LORD "knew face to face" (Deuteronomy 34:10). Nothing in the text says the thing that set him apart was a flawless record, and I think that's good news for us. It's about being known by God and serving Him. When my stamps were blurry and I was stuck in the back of a drawer, that was still true of me, and it's still true of you on your roughest day.

And then the work keeps going. Joshua is filled with the spirit of wisdom, and the Israelites obey him and do as the LORD had commanded Moses (Deuteronomy 34:9). One servant finishes, and the LORD has the next one ready. So here's my question for you, baker: what has God put in your hands today? Do it faithfully, trust Him with the part you can't see the end of, and know the story isn't over yet.
